Hi Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks again for the call today — good to walk through the integration shape. A quick summary of what we expect from our side:

- Production baseline: ~10M tokens/day (customer-facing features, auto-responses).
- Expected average monthly usage: ~300M tokens.
- Peak/burst windows: up to ~100M tokens/day during promotions (short windows, ~2–6 hours).
- Target unit economics: ideally around $12–$18 per 1M tokens (this is our internal target for the feature economics).

Two quick asks:
1) What does Redwood’s rate-limit / quota model look like for short-term bursts? Can we get temporary quota increases for launch windows?
2) What are overage pricing and billing mechanics if we exceed a committed baseline?

I attached a quick traffic forecast (acme-traffic-forecast.csv) for reference. Our procurement contact (cc’d on follow-ups) is Kate (kate.procurement@acme.com).

Appreciate any concrete examples / numbers so we can model costs.

—John

John — thanks for the details and the CSV. Quick recap from our side and next steps below.

Recap / assumptions based on call + forecast:
- Baseline commit to model against: 300M tokens / month.
- Short bursts: up to ~100M tokens/day for 2–6 hour windows during promotions.
- Traffic pattern: mostly reads/generation (low average output token length per call), some spikes tied to campaigns.

Redwood options that map to your asks:
1) Quota model and burst behavior
   - Committed baseline: we’ll provision a monthly committed quota (e.g., 300M tokens). That quota is your predictable bucket.
   - Burst windows: we allow temporary quota increases for planned events — submit a support/ops request with the window and expected delta. For short, unplanned bursts we allow best-effort bursts if capacity is available.
   - Sustained increases (multi-day) require 48–72 hours notice to adjust reserved capacity.

2) Overage & burst pricing (illustrative):
   - Committed baseline unit price: $12 / 1M tokens (for a 300M/month commit).
   - Overage (uncommitted usage beyond baseline): $25 / 1M tokens.
   - Burst premium when we need immediate, unplanned capacity >2x committed peak: $35 / 1M tokens for that burst window.
   - We can discuss a capped burst allowance or a one-time free trial of increased quota for your launch week (see next steps).

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael to send a formal one-page pricing sheet (attached) and a suggested addendum for burst handling.
- If procurement is happy with the numbers, we’ll produce a formal quote and MSA (DocuSign).
- For your upcoming launch, we can provision a temporary quota increase for the launch week pending signed SOW or addendum. Need a confirmation of expected dates and peak multiplier (e.g., 2x–3x).

Attaching: redwood-pricing.pdf (illustrative). Rafael — can you confirm these numbers and add any timing SLA language for quota increases?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi John / Marissa,

Thanks — adding a few specifics so ACME’s finance/procurement can model cost and the operations team knows the cadence.

Pricing (finalizable on signature of a monthly commit):
- Commit tier: 300M tokens / month -> unit price $12 / 1M tokens (billed monthly).
- Overage: usage beyond the 300M commit billed at $25 / 1M tokens.
- Burst handling: for short, immediate bursts under 72 hours we can provide up to 2x baseline throughput without reservation, subject to capacity; overages during those bursts billed at $35 / 1M tokens.
- If you want guaranteed burst capacity (reserved bump), we can structure a short-term reserve for the window at an agreed uplift (negotiable) to achieve a lower burst rate.

Other mechanics:
- Quota increase lead time: 48 hours for multi-day increases; same-day temporary bumps are possible but on best-effort basis and not guaranteed.
- Monitoring: we’ll add token-level alerts to your Console project and notify when usage approaches 80% of committed quota.
- Billing: overage will be prorated into the next monthly invoice and appear as a separate line item.

Attachments included: redwood-pricing.pdf, master-services-agreement.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567 (RDW-ACME-2314)

If this aligns with ACME’s expectations, I can draft a short addendum that explicitly covers: quota bump process, burst premium, one-time launch-week temporary uplift (dates required), and a capped pilot credit if you’d like to test bursts.
